implementation_notes: For the dominant case - a concurrent keyed map - the BCL already implements the pattern: ConcurrentDictionary<TKey,TValue> uses an internal striped lock array (growable through its growLockArray flag) and exposes atomic compound operations such as GetOrAdd and AddOrUpdate, so no stripe array is written by hand. For keyed state that is not a dictionary (files, connections, sessions), the manual realization is an array of System.Threading.Lock values indexed by a stable hash and entered with the lock keyword; System.Threading.Lock is the .NET 9+ replacement for locking on an object and supports using-scoped entry.
pitfalls: GetHashCode is not stable across processes for string keys (randomized hashing) and changes for mutable keys; derive a stable stripe index yourself for keys that outlive one run.
A lock must not span await: the continuation may resume on another thread. Use SemaphoreSlim.WaitAsync or an AsyncKeyedLock-style library for async keyed serialization.
ConcurrentDictionary's per-key atomic operations do not make multi-step check-then-act sequences atomic; keep such sequences under one stripe lock or express them as a single GetOrAdd/AddOrUpdate.
